label: <DEL> in short sequences, or input w early in the original phase
explanation: Fires only at steps t=1..7, peaking at t=4, and never during the copy phase. Two contexts carry the activation mass. (1) The <DEL> step, 65% of mass. The rate falls steeply with sequence length: 7% of delimiter steps at L=3, 4% at L=4, under 1% for L>=6. (2) The input token w in the original phase, 30% of mass, rate about 9%. The strongest activations are on a second w that directly follows another w (e.g. j j j w [w]). g, z, e and t give weak activations. Activation is higher when earlier inputs were letters such as w/g/e/z/n and lower when digits appeared (66% of mass is in sequences with no digits), which suggests a graded readout of the hidden state rather than a crisp rule. Precision is low (~0.3): most short-sequence <DEL> steps and most early w inputs do not fire. Never fires on other tokens or at t=0.
